stage_a.note: Both founders maintain strong, positive engagement; Mama O smiles cheerfully while describing the product.
Kheedim lists the actions of making kimchi with sustained, energetic engagement.
Mama O makes a friendly OK sign and smiles warmly at the panel.

venture.description: Premium packaged kimchi and a homemade kimchi-making kit that reduces preparation time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim introduces himself and his mother Mama O, seeking $250,000 for a 10% equity stake in Mama O's Premium Kimchi.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O greets the sharks warmly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim introduces his pregnant wife Amy as a co-owner of the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O describes kimchi as an ancient Korean superfood that is naturally fermented and full of probiotics.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim lists foods that kimchi pairs well with, emphasizing its incredible taste.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim highlights that their authentic Korean mom recipe makes their kimchi the best.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O bows gracefully to the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim explains their innovative packaging and introduces their homemade kimchi kit that reduces preparation time to under ten minutes.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O reassures the panel that making kimchi is a lot easier than they might think.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim asks the sharks who is interested in fermenting some money with them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori praises their presentation and states that she loves kimchi.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim invites Daymond to come up and help Mama O make some kimchi.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond accepts the invitation, stating it would be an honor.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O welcomes Daymond and jokes that making kimchi is like sex education but spicier.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O asks Daymond to put on a rubber glove.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond jokes about needing rubber gloves during sex education.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O explains that making kimchi starts with a head of napa cabbage.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond repeats the Korean word for napa cabbage to confirm.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O instructs Daymond to add a jar of kimchi paste and scoop it out with his fingers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond confirms if he has added enough paste.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O tells Daymond to mix and gently toss the cabbage and paste lovingly.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokes that he is getting turned on by Daymond's mixing.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O announces the kimchi is ready for fermentation and can be eaten fresh like a salad.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond tastes the freshly mixed kimchi and remarks that it is sweet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O shows the finished jar of kimchi to the panel.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks about the function of the airlock on the top of the jar.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O explains that the airlock allows the kimchi to breathe while it is fermenting.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond thanks her and says he feels warm and fuzzy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim points out the samples provided to the sharks, noting there are four different kimchis.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks for clarification, believing there was only one type of kimchi.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim explains there are hundreds of types and details the specific varieties they provided.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks Daymond if he tried the super spicy version.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim mentions he was just about to warn Daymond about the super spicy kimchi.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond confirms that the super spicy kimchi is indeed very hot.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kendra asks the founders how they came up with the idea for the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim shares his origin story of asking his mom for kimchi, transporting it on a skateboard, and eventually selling it.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks about the production costs and retail prices for their products.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim provides the costs and wholesale and retail prices for both the packaged kimchi and the kit.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks Kheedim to share their sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim states that their top-line sales for the previous year were $815,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for their projected sales for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim projects their sales will reach one million dollars this year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks what their profit margin will be.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim replies that their profit margin is 25%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kendra asks if the majority of their sales come from Whole Foods or direct-to-consumer channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim clarifies they have almost zero online sales and mentions their partnership with Williams Sonoma.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks how long they have been selling in Whole Foods.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim estimates they have been in Whole Foods for about eight years.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark challenges Kheedim on why their sales are not higher given their time in business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim explains he built the company from scratch with no outside investors, doing everything himself.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark presses further, asking what specific obstacles are holding the company back from reaching higher revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim admits his belief was to only hire more people after making money, avoiding outside funding.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if Kheedim pays himself a salary from the profits they are making.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim confirms he does not pay himself and reinvests all profits back into the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kendra asks Mama O how she feels seeing her son build the business from nothing.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O expresses deep pride in her son's hard work, honesty, and the recent addition of his wife.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kendra tells Mama O that her sentiments are truly beautiful.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that bringing such a supportive mother to the pitch is an unfair advantage.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits, citing the difficult challenge of educating consumers to try the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, feeling Kheedim waited too long to hire and would struggle to delegate effectively.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori exits, stating that despite loving the founders and the product, the business is not investable for her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kendra exits, explaining she cannot invest because she does not personally consume or stand behind kimchi.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks why Kheedim feels ready now to change his family-run operation and take an investor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kheedim explains that expecting a new baby next month creates a need for additional income.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mama O adds that the company needs an investor's expertise and guidance to reach a larger market.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond exits, trusting his gut that while he loves their culture, he is not obsessed with the product.

decisions.note: Feels it requires too much consumer education to get people to try the product.
Believes the founder waited too long to hire and will struggle to delegate to employees.
Loves the founders and the product but does not find the business investable for her.
Needs to stand behind what she sells and is not personally a consumer of kimchi.
Loves the culture but is not obsessed with the product, choosing to trust his gut.

record.notes: The prepared presentation spans multiple turns due to continuous back-and-forth delivery between the two founders.
